lem-odd-cube-oriented-face-parity-and-si.actual_quote: 1.1 **The two-saddle calculation.** Quotients commute with quotients. Two split factors anticommute because $u\wedge v=-v\wedge u$. A quotient and a split commute when the quotient carries the split difference to the corresponding output difference. These give $\kappa=1,-1,1$, respectively, for two merges, two splits and a mixed pair whose saddle types are unchanged by interchange. The remaining connected nonzero case starts with two circles and two bands between them: either order first merges and then splits. Both composites factor through the quotient identifying the two input circles. If the two band arrows point towards the same input circle, their final split differences are opposites, giving $\kappa=-1$; if they point towards different circles, the differences agree, giving $\kappa=1$. Finally, alternating endpoints on a single input circle give a split followed by a merge in either order. The quotient kills the split difference, so both composites are zero. These exhaust the cases: discard components missing both arcs, and distinguish whether each arc joins equal or distinct components; if both are self-arcs, their endpoints either alternate or do not. A spectator generator is carried identically throughout, so the computation on the incident generators proves the full exterior-map equation. [F1, given, algebra]

lem-odd-cube-oriented-face-parity-and-si.actual_quote: 2.2 **Separating a configuration.** Collapse each saddle disk to a four-valent vertex and retain the regular arcs joining its four ports. Discard vertex-free circles. This gives a planar four-valent multigraph with three vertices. If it is disconnected, one component contains just one vertex. If it has a two-edge cut, cut those edges and cap the resulting pair of ports in each piece by an arc. The original diagram is then obtained by joining the two capped marked arcs; one piece again has one vertex and the other two. The caps can be chosen in a thin neighbourhood of the cut, so they preserve the cyclic orders and inside/outside intersection test for every two-saddle face within a piece. Every resolution of the joined diagram has the circle count $k_1+k_2-1$; in the disconnected case it has count $k_1+k_2$. lem-odd-marked-reidemeister-i-ii-contrac.actual_quote: 1.1 **A cancellation identity over any ring.** Suppose a cochain differential $d$ on $M=A\oplus B\oplus R$ has a degree-one block $b:A\to B$ which is an isomorphism. Set $h|_B=b^{-1}$ and $h|_{A\oplus R}=0$. Then $h^2=0$ and $hdh=h$. Consequently $E=1-dh-hd$ is a projection commuting with $d$: expansion using $d^2=h^2=0$ and $hdh=h$ gives $E^2=E$ and $dE=Ed$. Writing $j:R\to M$ and $q:M\to R$ for the direct-sum maps, set $i=Ej=j-hdj$, $p=qE=q-qdh$, and $d_R=q(d-dhd)j$. The $A$-coordinate of a vector in $\operatorname{im}E$ is minus $hd$ of its $R$-coordinate, and its $B$-coordinate is zero; hence $q:\operatorname{im}E\to R$ and $Ej$ are inverse. Thus $pi=1$, $ip=E$, $di=id_R$, $pd=d_Rp$, and $1-ip=dh+hd$. These identities also give $d_R^2=0$. If the blocks and their inverse are right-module maps, so are all these maps. This calculation applies to entire finite exterior cubes at once; their differentials are included in $d$, rather than omitted as spectators. [given, algebra, construct]

In state $10$ label the circle through the upper arc $a$, the small circle $z$, and the circle through the lower arc $c$; the exterior closure may identify $a$ and $c$. The normalization makes the survivor's cohomological and quantum degrees those of the old diagram: the extra small circle and extra exterior generator change the local quantum degree by $-1$, cancelling the positive-curl shift $+1$. Thus $\Lambda V=\Lambda U\otimes\mathbb A$ as a right module, by $u\otimes1\mapsto u$, $u\otimes X\mapsto u\wedge Z$. A merge preserves augmentation and takes the marked generator to the marked generator. For a split choose the lift of its old marked generator to the new marked generator; if the marked circle is unaffected this is the usual lift. This lift also preserves augmentation, and the split difference belongs to $U$ in the target. Hence in these coordinates every edge acts as its reduced exterior quotient or split on $\Lambda U$, tensored with the identity of $\mathbb A$. This is an equality of maps on both $u$ and $u\wedge Z$, not merely an unmarked abelian-group splitting. [F1, algebra, construct]

At a joined state the reduced difference group is $U_1\oplus U_2$, by sending every $Z_i-Z_j^{\mathrm{mark}}$ to its difference from the merged marked generator. thm-leo-local-equivalence-group-and-conc.actual_quote: 3.1 For $T=(C,D,f)$ define $T^*=(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb A}(C,\mathbb A)\{2\},\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(D,\mathbb R)\{2\},f^*)$, where $f^*$ is the transpose induced by a homotopy inverse $g$ to the reduced equivalence $f$. Finite freeness lets dualization commute with reduction and localization; it preserves chain homotopies and chain homotopy equivalences. Thus $T^*$ satisfies the LEO conditions, and dualizing both maps and the module-linear homotopy in a local-map square gives a local map in the reverse direction. The finite-free tensor-Hom isomorphisms identify $T\otimes T^*$ with $(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb A}(C,C)\{1\},\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(D,D)\{1\},F)$, where on reductions $F(\eta)=f\eta g$. The coevaluation maps from the unknot triple send $1$ to $\mathrm{id}_C$ and $\mathrm{id}_D$. The reduced square commutes up to the module-linear homotopy $H$ from $fg\simeq\mathrm{id}_D$, since $F(\mathrm{id}_C)=fg$. After inverting $h$, the BN coevaluation map $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R[h^{-1}]}(D[h^{-1}],D[h^{-1}])$ sends $1$ to $\mathrm{id}_D$; under a chosen homotopy equivalence $D[h^{-1}]\simeq\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ it is homotopic to the identity map of the rank-one endomorphism complex, so it is a homotopy equivalence by [F2]. The reverse evaluation maps are the graded evaluations $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(c)$ on the finite-free tensor-Hom identifications, with the standard Hom differential $d\phi=-(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi d$. They are chain maps because the two terms in $d(\phi\otimes c)$ evaluate to $-(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi(dc)$ and $+(-1)^{|\phi|}\phi(dc)$. For the reduced evaluation square choose a separate module-linear homotopy $\ell$ on $\bar C=C\otimes\mathbb F_2$ satisfying $gf-\mathrm{id}_{\bar C}=d\ell+\ell d$; the homotopy $H$ above acts on $\bar D$ and is not used here. Under the graded flip to the dual-first tensor order, the two reduced evaluation composites are $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(c)$ and $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(gf(c))$, so the reduced square commutes up to $\phi\otimes c\mapsto\phi(\ell(c))$ (over $\mathbb F_2$ the Koszul signs are one), and after localization evaluation identifies with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R[h^{-1}]}(\mathbb R[h^{-1}],\mathbb R[h^{-1}])\to\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$, an isomorphism. Hence the two evaluation maps are local maps in both directions, proving $T\otimes T^*$ locally equivalent to the unknot triple and $T^*$ is an inverse. Finite tensor-Hom associativity, the graded flip, and the unknot's identity endomorphism give associativity, commutativity and the unit, so local-equivalence classes form an abelian group. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra, construct]

def-odd-khovanov-barnatan-and-leo-triple.actual_quote: Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented knot diagram with ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ and a marked point $p$ away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

def-odd-khovanov-barnatan-and-leo-triple.actual_quote: Put $\mathbb B=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)=\mathbb R/(2,h)$. Modulo $2$, the odd exterior basis vector $C_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge C_{i_r}$ corresponds to the even tensor state labeling the selected circles $C_{i_j}$ by $X$ and all other circles by $1$. This statewise bijection defines the candidate comparison $f_D:C_o(D)\otimes\mathbb F_2\to C_h(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B$ after setting $h=0$.

def-odd-khovanov-barnatan-and-leo-triple.actual_quote:
A **local even–odd (LEO) triple** is a triple $(C,D,f)$ consisting of a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $C$ free over $\mathbb A$, a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $D$ free over $\mathbb R$, and a bigraded $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy equivalence
$$ f:C\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_2\longrightarrow D\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B, \qquad \mathbb B=\mathbb R/(2,h)=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2), $$
such that $D[h^{-1}]$ is chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ to one free rank-one module supported in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree. For a based knot diagram the intended candidate is $(C_o(D),C_h(D),f_D)$, where $f_D$ identifies the reduced edge maps modulo $2$ and $h$; its satisfaction of the homotopy and localization conditions is a separate theorem.
def-odd-khovanov-barnatan-and-leo-triple.assessment: Definition:leo-conditions and Definition:local-map-conditions specify data and equivalence, not a proved iff criterion. Proof3.1 defers the separate knot realization.
